reviewed: module.json (full walk of S1 to S8 and END, every probe, trap feedback, hint and explain node; claims read)
gate_check: G3: every next target in S1 to S8 resolves to a defined node; no dead ends found; every explain node has a forward or retry exit; the END node is reached from S8.q10_ok. G4: buttons only, no typing, no run-time model.

segments.reason: Probe first on the GSV/SFJ and primary-type ideas; TR7 and TR19 options each name the model, sure_notes refute it, and the S1.check contrast separates the two saphenous veins by side and termination. Skip lane at S1.gate_ok and S1.check.

Flow, pump and vignette probes are well built (S2.p_flow_t2 is a good refutation). But S2.p_named is probed with no teach node, and its feedback says 'the medial-leg names you have just heard', which is untrue on this path. S2.p_vig key is the longest option, findable by form.

Clinical probes (ulcer type, site, CEAP diameter, class, skin subclass) use vignettes with a hint each and single-model traps. Weak point: S3.varix_t24a asks a question and offers only Try again, so the shared-thrill belief is not refuted (S7.p8_t0 does this properly).

Worked case S4.wex1 then faded probe S4.wex2 is a strong ladder; tourniquet and test-ladder probes contrast each pair with an agency path to S4.tq2_why and S4.inv_why. S4.seq_t4 maps a 'junction test is the go-ahead' belief to TR4, which is a name-swap trap, so the report cannot name the model.

S5.err1 is internally inconsistent: two of the three wrong steps (step 3, foam if ablation is unsuitable; step 4, open surgery only if both fail) are correct by the module's own worked plan at S5.worked and S5.open_ok. A learner who picks them is told they are wrong, and S5.err1_t21 teaches a false lesson about foam. S5.vig key is the only option without 'foam'.

Case A/B/C/D bridge and the ulcer, ABPI, deep-patency and nerve sequence are clinically authentic and the traps are real (TR16, TR18, TR8, TR9). But nine explain nodes (S6.ex_site to S6.ex_nr) offer only Try again, the key of S6.pExtent and S6.pSite is the odd-shaped option, and S6.ex_tx uses 'EVRA' unexpanded.

Ten 'which is NOT correct' drills in a row. The concept coverage is good (eponyms, CEAP, tests, sclerosants), but every trap is a true statement and the feedback opens 'That choice is not right. It is true', a contradiction to a tired reader. No interleaved teaching; the drills re-ask S1 to S6 beliefs. S7.p8_t0 is the best refutation in the segment.

Cold consolidation with no hint options on q6 to q10, as intended. Several probes are two options or have a findable key (S8.q6 'to protect the saphenous nerve', S8.q10 'still needed'). S8.q3 and S8.q5 traps are good and map to their models.

best_parts: node S1.check with S1.check_t7a and S1.check_why: a contrast probe in which each look-alike changes one attribute (side or termination); the feedback names the swap and gives the side-first rule.
node S2.p_flow_t2 with its sure_note: names the tempting belief (the squeeze is the direction), separates force from gate, and the learner keeps the reasoning, not just the answer.

node S4.wex1 into S4.wex2 and S4.wex2_t5: a worked case with every step shown, then a faded probe where each wrong option is one structure, and the filling-after-release rule is stated before the retest.
node S4.tq2_why: a side-by-side maneuver contrast of Perthes and Brodie-Trendelenburg, reached from both the sure and agency paths on S4.tq2_t1 and S4.tq2_t2.
node S7.p8_t0: the TR24 feedback refutes the shared-sign belief with the varix-hernia discriminator (cough shared, fluid thrill not). This is the refutation S3.varix_t24a should carry.
flaws: node S5.err1 (options S5.err1_t21 and S5.err1_t1): the trap steps 3 and 4 are correct by the module's own plan (S5.worked: foam next if ablation unsuitable; open surgery only if both unsuitable). A learner who picks them is marked wrong for a correct step, and S5.err1_t21 ('Foam is not limited to small veins') teaches a false lesson. Replace them with genuinely wrong steps (for example foam as first-line for a trunk, or surgery first) so each wrong option is one trap (R2, R9, R4).

node S2.p_named_t1 and S2.p_named: the four perforator names are probed with no teach node before the probe, but the feedback says 'one of the medial-leg names you have just heard'. On this path nothing was heard. Add an explain node that lists Cockett, Boyd, Dodd and Hunter by level before S2.p_named, or reword to 'the medial-leg names' (R1, R4).

node S3.varix_t24a: the feedback ends with a question ('Which feature in this case does not fit a hernia?') and offers only Try again. The shared-thrill belief is never refuted, so the learner reaches the key by elimination. Carry the refutation of S7.p8_t0 (both lumps have a cough impulse; the fluid thrill separates them) and add a Show me why exit (R2, R5).

node S4.seq_t4: the label 'A positive Brodie-Trendelenburg test' is mapped to TR4 (test-name swap), but the wrong model is 'a junction test result is the go-ahead to operate'. The trap and the model do not match, so the report cannot name the belief. Map it to TR18 or add a trap for it (R9).

nodes S6.ex_site, S6.ex_abpi, S6.ex_tx, S6.ex_deep, S6.ex_dv, S6.ex_ext, S6.ex_why, S6.ex_n and S6.ex_nr: each explanation offers only 'Try again', which returns the learner to the same stem with no forward move and no second explanation. Add a Next to the following probe, or a delayed re-test in a new form (R5).

node S6.pSite and S6.pExtent: the key is the only option of a different shape ('Unlikely venous; check the arterial supply first' and 'From the groin to just below the knee'), while the traps are parallel. The key is findable by form. Rebalance the wording (R2).

node S2.p_vig, S8.q3, S8.q10 and S8.q6: the key is the longest option in each (S2.p_vig 'from reflux or blocked deep veins', S8.q3 'and reflux stops it falling', S8.q10 'still needed before ablation'), and S8.q6 has only two options with the key the only one with a purpose. Pad or trim the options so the key is not marked by length (R2).
node S3.case: both traps end in a 'since' clause and the key does not, so the key is marked by form. Give all three options the same clause shape (R2).

node S5.vig and S5.vig_h: the key is the only option that does not mention foam, and the hint ('these are the smallest veins in the stem') nearly gives the answer. Make the foam and liquid options parallel and cut the hint to a question about vein size (R2).

segment S7 (nodes S7.p1 to S7.p10): ten 'which is NOT correct' probes in a row. Every trap is a true statement, and each trap feedback opens 'That choice is not right. It is true...', which reads as a contradiction to a tired learner. Reword the opener to name the choice ('That one is true, so it is the wrong pick here'), interleave a teach node or skip lane, and vary the form (R4, R8, R1).
node S6.ex_tx: 'the EVRA result' is an unexpanded acronym with no explanation. Expand it the first time it appears (DP25; R4).

report.json, trap TR18 'fell_recovered': 'You first treated a positive Perthes as reassuring, then reversed' describes a belief no TR18 option in this module offers (S4.seq_t18 'reflux is enough', S6.pDeep 'perforator competence', S6.t_deep2 'a varix is the precondition', S8.q5_t18 'deep veins do not matter'). The trap lines are template text assigned by first encounter only, so a misconceived learner is told the wrong model (R9).

report.json and sim/misconceived.report.json: the headline is 'mixed' and all twelve objective tiers are 'shaky', regardless of the cold-quiz result (9 of 11 right, per the sim). next_steps says to start with 'gap objectives', but no objective is in the gap tier, so the learner cannot tell which card to start with. Use the cold-quiz results and the tier spread to set secure versus shaky, and name the first card (R9).

report.json and sim/misconceived.report.json, help: 'hints' counts the 'Show me why' explanation taps (14), and the hints_heavy text then tells the learner they asked for hints often. Count hint taps and explanation taps separately (R9).

report_check.headline: mixed does not match a walk that refuted every trap and answered most cold stems right. It should name the first qualifier to fix (the PYQ key versus current practice for treatment, and the deep-vein check before superficial surgery) and mention the cold quiz.
report_check.objectives: All twelve tiers read shaky, so the objective texts carry no information. Tier from the cold quiz and the first-encounter outcomes; name the one gap if there is one.
report_check.traps: Trap lines are template wording assigned by first encounter. TR18 describes a belief this module never offers. Retry-only falls (for example S3.varix_t24a) are not reported separately from recovered falls.
report_check.calibration: overconfident is plausible for a misconceived walk. The sure_wrong count (23) and guess_right (0) are not checked here; the sim's own count differs by one.
report_check.help: hints 14 counts explanation taps. Separate hint taps from Show me why taps; the hints_heavy text is misleading for this path.
report_check.next_steps: The card order is useful, but the 'gap objectives' wording points at a tier nothing reached. Name the cards, in order, from the trap lines and the cold result.

personas_checked.misconceived: rendered report judged. The trap lines name the right confusion for most traps, which is the strongest part. The TR18 line describes the wrong belief, the headline and tiers ignore the cold quiz, and the help count misstates this learner's help use. Useful in parts, not accurate enough to set the next step.
personas_checked.novice, strong, guesser: no sim report for these personas exists in the workshop, not judged.

sim_check.misconceived: The path separates each wrong model at the point of choice in S1 to S4 and in S8, and the explain nodes help most in S4 and S5. The weak stretches are S5.err1 (correct steps trapped), S6 (retry-only explanations) and S7 (ten NOT drills in a row). The sim's own verdict (engagement 3 of 5) fits this reading.

merge_ideas: Use the S5.worked then S5.err1 pattern for S6: a worked case first, then one faded probe per step, each wrong option a single trap with a forward Next after the explanation.
Interleave S7: alternate each NOT drill with a one-screen teach or a skip lane, and make trap feedback refute the belief the way S7.p8_t0 does, not with 'It is true'.
Carry S7.p8_t0's refutation into S3.varix_t24a, and S4.wex1's worked-case framing into S2 before the perforator-name probe, so each weak node gets a second explanation in a different form.
Make the report tiers depend on the cold quiz (S8 results): refuted then answered cold is secure; refuted then missed cold is shaky; name the first card in the headline.
unscored_notes: Not gated. No typing and no run-time model. Facts are not judged (CLAUDE.md). Node word counts were read by eye and look within 60 words; no structural validator was run. The trauma review.json was read only for format; its content is about another module and was not used for scoring.
